claim: CodeVetter can compare bounded integrity-checked browser-probe recaptures without rerunning the application and withhold a follow-up when repeated routes disagree.

policy.stable_route_requirement: same non-null classification and next probe in every included run
policy.follow_up_requirement: stable route and passed correctness in every included run

boundaries: fixed local probe and Playwright receipt locations only
regular non-symlink files with linked receipt and result digest validation
exact source snapshot, source probe, request, flow, project, presentation profile, runtime, and completed-evidence compatibility
read-only operation with no browser, application, local runtime, production, or cloud execution

interpretation: The earlier single-run routes were not reproducible across two compatible recaptures. CodeVetter now exposes that instability instead of allowing an agent to choose the more actionable-looking branch. Two runs cannot establish stability even when they agree; a third unanimous repetition is required.
limitations: The CPU-ratio threshold is retained as observed context; proximity does not prove that the threshold caused the disagreement.
Both exact browser assertions failed, independently blocking follow-up eligibility.
This is local repeated evidence and establishes no production frequency, latency, scale, user impact, bottleneck, source cause, or optimization.
